references.text: Also describes gold rings for the table in the tabernacle, which were to be placed at the feet to hold the carrying poles, following the same construction principle as the ark.
Gold rings used in the construction of the tabernacle to hold crossbars show a consistent design pattern with rings for transport and stability.
Bronze rings on the altar of burnt offering for carrying poles, with the same functional design as the gold rings on the ark.
Gold rings on the incense altar for carrying poles, a parallel construction to the ark of the covenant.
Fulfillment of the instruction in 25:12, where Bezalel actually cast the four gold rings and attached them to the four feet of the ark.
Parallel execution of gold rings for the table of showbread, using the same craftsmanship technique as for the ark.
Instructions for the Levites transporting the holy objects of the tabernacle using the carrying poles that passed through the rings.
The ark of the covenant with its carrying poles is brought into the temple; the rings made this transport possible from the City of David to Solomon's temple.
This is a parallel instruction for the same object (the table) given to Moses before its execution.
